basisClaims.statement: A paired t procedure analyzes within-pair differences for continuous repeated or matched measurements when those differences are reasonably normal.

basisClaims.applicablePopulation: Fictional educational and quality-improvement datasets with the assumptions stated in each question.

basisClaims.statement: One-way analysis of variance compares means across independent groups when the observations, residual distribution, and variance assumptions are reasonable.
basisClaims.limitation: A significant omnibus result does not identify which groups differ; post-hoc procedures are outside this objective.
basisClaims.applicablePopulation: Fictional educational and quality-improvement datasets with the assumptions stated in each question.

basisClaims.statement: The Wilcoxon rank-sum procedure compares ranked observations from two independent groups; its interpretation is not automatically an unqualified comparison of medians.
basisClaims.limitation: Shape and location assumptions affect interpretation; the content does not claim that rank-sum testing always tests medians.
basisClaims.applicablePopulation: Fictional educational and quality-improvement datasets with the assumptions stated in each question.

basisClaims.statement: The Wilcoxon signed-rank procedure ranks nonzero paired differences and relies on a reasonably symmetric difference distribution for its usual location interpretation.
basisClaims.limitation: The fictional exercises explicitly state symmetry; a simple sign procedure may be preferable when that assumption is not reasonable.
basisClaims.applicablePopulation: Fictional educational and quality-improvement datasets with the assumptions stated in each question.

basisClaims.statement: A chi-square test of independence assesses association between categorical variables when independent observations and adequate expected counts support its approximation.
basisClaims.limitation: Sparse tables may require an exact method; the exercises state that expected counts are adequate.
basisClaims.applicablePopulation: Fictional educational and quality-improvement datasets with the assumptions stated in each question.

basisClaims.statement: Fisher exact testing provides an exact analysis of a two-by-two categorical table when sparse expected counts make a chi-square approximation unreliable.
basisClaims.limitation: The exercises are confined to sparse two-by-two tables and do not generalize the method to every categorical analysis.
basisClaims.applicablePopulation: Fictional educational and quality-improvement datasets with the assumptions stated in each question.

basisClaims.statement: McNemar testing is for paired binary responses, so it does not fit independent, continuous, ordinal, or multi-category observations in these exercises.
